body.statement: There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\beta,L,G,H,\underline f,\overline f)\), such that for all even \(T\ge32\) and \(B\ge1\), \[cF_\alpha(T,b)\le R_T(B)\le CF_\alpha(T,b).\] The upper inequality is attained by the implementable hard-cap policy \(\pi^\star\), and the lower inequality holds over all \(\Pi_{T,B}\).
body.justification: The matched upper and lower bounds are the theorem-level design certificate: they identify the exact cost of memory and a common deadline.
body.gap: No named comparator simultaneously imposes deterministic capacity, arrival-incidence matching, terminal perfect pairing, and additive causal precision regret over a Hölder class.
body.consumer: Trial designers obtain a capacity calculator that is minimax-certified rather than tuned only by simulation.

obligation.what_is_open: The all-regime upper inequality and its attaining policy remain unproved because the sibling-owned endpoint-safe coarsening question has not yet supplied the required hard-cap clearance estimate.
obligation.obstruction: The proved capped-grid policy pays a terminal residual-cell charge of order \(m/T\). After optimizing over \(m\), this can exceed the harmonic deadline term in the claimed frontier when \(b\) is large relative to \(T\). The frozen primitives contain no result controlling inherited residues during arrival-incidence coarsening, and this unit does not own the endpoint-safe coarsening open-ended question.
obligation.attempted: I combined the proved all-policy converse with the capped-grid upper theorem and optimized its explicit bound. Choosing \(m=b\) closes the theorem when \(b^{1+\alpha}\le T\), but outside that regime the optimized capped-grid expression is not uniformly bounded by the claimed frontier. A deterministic merging argument cannot pair two already-stored residues under the arrival-incidence rule, so it does not establish terminal clearing.
obligation.partial_result:
The established converse and the capped-grid construction give
\[
cF_\alpha(T,b)
\le R_T(B)
\le C\inf_{1\le m\le b}\left\{m^{-\alpha}+\frac{m}{T}\right\}.
\]
If \(b^{1+\alpha}\le T\), choosing \(m=b\) and using \(b/T\le b^{-\alpha}\le F_\alpha(T,b)\) gives
\[
cF_\alpha(T,b)\le R_T(B)\le 2C F_\alpha(T,b).
\]
Thus the claimed frontier is proved in the capacity-dominated regime.  For general \(b\), the all-policy lower bound remains valid, but the available upper bound need not be within a constant factor of \(F_\alpha(T,b)\).  A pathwise hard-cap, terminal-empty policy with expected inherited-clearance cost of order \(\sum_{r=1}^b r^{-\alpha}\) is the remaining step needed for the theorem as stated.
